headline: Iran Conflict Doubles Egypt LNG Import Bill Amid Declining Output
summary: The war on Iran doubled Egypt's liquefied natural gas import bill as domestic gas output fell to 3.63 billion cubic feet per day in August, forcing Cairo to defer cargoes and burn fuel oil.
why: Energy importing nations face severe fiscal and current account strains when geopolitical conflicts disrupt global supply and drive up liquefied natural gas prices.
why_moved: Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East severely restricts regional energy supplies, spiking the cost of imported LNG for dependent nations.
